### CVE-2024-0153 — Mali GPU Firmware allows improper GPU processing operations
- Assigner: Arm | Published: 2024-07-01 | Updated: 2024-08-01 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: CWE-119 CWE-119 Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer vulnerability in Arm Ltd Valhall GPU Firmware, Arm Ltd Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Firmware allows a local non-privileged user to make improper GPU processing operations to access a limited amount outside of buffer bounds. If the operations are carefully prepared, then this in turn could give them access to all system memory. This issue affects Valhall GPU Firmware: from r29p0 through r46p0; Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Firmware: from r41p0 through r46p0.

**solutions:** This issue is fixed in Valhall and Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Firmware r47p0. Users are recommended to upgrade if they are impacted by this issue.

Affected:
- Arm Ltd / Valhall GPU Firmware: affected r29p0 <=r46p0 (patch) changes:unaffected@r47p0
- Arm Ltd / Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Firmware: affected r41p0 <=r46p0 (patch) changes:unaffected@r47p0
- arm / valhall_gpu_kernel_driver: affected r29p0 <r46p0 (custom)
- arm / 5th_gen_gpu_architecture_kernel_driver: affected r41p0 <r46p0 (custom)

References:
- https://developer.arm.com/Arm%20Security%20Center/Mali%20GPU%20Driver%20Vulnerabilities

### CVE-2024-1067 — Mali GPU Kernel Driver allows improper GPU memory processing operations
- Assigner: Arm | Published: 2024-05-03 | Updated: 2025-03-27 | Max CVSS: 7.4
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Use After Free vulnerability in Arm Ltd Bifrost GPU Kernel Driver, Arm Ltd Valhall GPU Kernel Driver, Arm Ltd Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Kernel Driver allows a local non-privileged user to make improper GPU memory processing operations. On Armv8.0 cores, there are certain combinations of the Linux Kernel and Mali GPU kernel driver configurations that would allow the GPU operations to affect the userspace memory of other processes.
This issue affects Bifrost GPU Kernel Driver: from r41p0 through r47p0; Valhall GPU Kernel Driver: from r41p0 through r47p0; Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Kernel Driver: from r41p0 through r47p0.



**solutions:** This issue is fixed in Bifrost, Valhall and Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Kernel Driver r48p0. Users are recommended to upgrade if they are impacted by this issue.  


Affected:
- Arm Ltd / Bifrost GPU Kernel Driver: affected r41p0 <=r47p0 (patch) changes:unaffected@r48p0
- Arm Ltd / Valhall GPU Kernel Driver: affected r41p0 <=r47p0 (patch) changes:unaffected@r48p0
- Arm Ltd / Arm 5th Gen GPU Architecture Kernel Driver: affected r41p0 <=r47p0 (patch) changes:unaffected@r48p0

### CVE-2024-6563 — Buffer Overflow Arbitrary Write
- Assigner: ASRG | Published: 2024-07-08 | Updated: 2024-08-01 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-123 CWE-123: Write-what-where Condition; CWE-120 CWE-120 Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow')
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability in Renesas arm-trusted-firmware allows Local Execution of Code. This vulnerability is associated with program files  https://github.Com/renesas-rcar/arm-trusted-firmware/blob/rcar_gen3_v2.5/drivers/renesas/common/io/i... https://github.Com/renesas-rcar/arm-trusted-firmware/blob/rcar_gen3_v2.5/drivers/renesas/common/io/io_rcar.C .




In line 313 "addr_loaded_cnt" is checked not to be "CHECK_IMAGE_AREA_CNT" (5) or larger, this check does not halt the function. Immediately after (line 317) there will be an overflow in the buffer and the value of "dst" will be written to the area immediately after the buffer, which is "addr_loaded_cnt". This will allow an attacker to freely control the value of "addr_loaded_cnt" and thus control the destination of the write immediately after (line 318). The write in line 318 will then be fully controlled by said attacker, with whichever address and whichever value ("len") they desire.

Affected:
- Renesas / rcar_gen3_v2.5: affected c2f286820471ed276c57e603762bd831873e5a17 <=c9fb3558410032d2660c7f3b7d4b87dec09fe2f2 (git) files: https://github.com/renesas-rcar/arm-trusted-firmware/blob/rcar_gen3_v2.5/drivers/renesas/common/io/io_rcar.c
- renesas / rcar_gen3_firmware: affected v2.5

Credits: Ilay levi

References:
- https://github.com/renesas-rcar/arm-trusted-firmware/commit/235f85b654a031f7647e81b86fc8e4ffeb430164
- https://asrg.io/security-advisories/cve-2024-6563/ [third-party-advisory]
